notes: Recovery-center release: system-level failures that used to need a terminal are now recoverable in the console. The new Recovery card shows the watchdog's health and escalation circuit, settings-file sanity (an unparsable file now SAYS 'running on defaults' instead of failing silently), the console's restart counters, clock-skew detection, retired session leftovers, old-log sizes, proxy mode and the dirty-worktree file names — diagnosis only, never auto-cleaning. One-click actions: restart the watchdog (recycled with its current config), retry an open escalation circuit (queued through the watchdog's new command channel, consumed at the next cycle), restart the console (the page answers 202 first, drops for a moment, and comes back), clean this product's own log files older than seven days, remove the two retired transition-era sessions, and a DIRECT MODE switch for a dead local proxy (machine-local proxy.local, applied on the next service restart, with the honest restart hint). Every action is Bearer-gated and lands in the event stream; nothing destructive is ever automated. Core grows to 2124/2124 tests, console smoke to 471/471, and locale packs to 1306 keys per language.
